label: input token v at original-phase position >= 4
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is v during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position t >= 4; precision 1.0 and recall ~1.0 on dev. Does not fire on v at positions 0-3, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase (including v fed back as copied input), and essentially never on other tokens (23 tiny activations ~0.02 of max, mostly the step right after a v at t>=4). Magnitude grows with position: about 0.3 of max at t=4, about 0.6-0.7 at t=5, about 0.97-1.0 at t=7, as seen in the examples. Independent of previous tokens, first token, sequence length (apart from long sequences having more eligible positions) and repeats.

issues: Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.9996, F1 0.9998, mass recall 0.99998. There are no false positives. The 18 missed steps hold about 0% of activation mass and are scattered tiny activations (0.01-0.04 of max) at step 7, mostly right after a v. That is noise, not a systematic class.
The phase claims hold: there are zero activations on the delimiter step and zero in the copy phase, including when v is fed back as input. There are also zero activations at t=0-3.

The magnitude claim is slightly imprecise. Per-t means worked out from activation-mass shares (max 3.31) are about 0.27 of max at t=4, 0.61 at t=5, 0.81 at t=6, 0.86 at t=7 and 0.85 at t=8. So magnitude grows and then levels off from about t=6-7; it does not keep increasing. The '0.97-1.0 at t=7' figure describes individual top examples, not the typical value. This is a minor issue and does not affect the label.
The firing rate given a v at original position >= 4 is flat at about 0.033 per orig_idx. This is consistent with the predicate being exact, with no dependence on length or history.
